text:
Juraj Slafkovsky hasn't scored in eleven games, and he has two goals all season. For a 22-year-old first overall pick who had 30 goals last season, that's the kind of number that starts conversations in Montreal. The answer from our numbers is patience.

He's still getting the chances. His expected goals (the quality of his own chances) over the last ten games are exactly his usual rate, 3.6, and on the season he has 2 goals on 7.1 expected. That gap almost always closes. He's also created plenty for others, 11 assists, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 88th percentile for setting up shots last season. Our talent range still projects about 20 goals.

The fair criticism is defensive. Montreal takes 49% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, a bit below the team, and Evolving-Hockey found opponents created more against him last season than against almost any forward, though he was facing top competition. With Kreider and Demidov out, he's up over 20 minutes a night. Arpon Basu of The Athletic wrote that the version of Slafkovsky from the Utah win needs to be the one Montreal sees from now on. The goals will help.
